meta.description: Template-sensitive half of a pair. The conversation is prebuilt so the model is not asked to call anything: an assistant turn already carries a tool_calls block, and a tool turn already carries the answer, keyed back by tool_call_id. The only work left is to read 'QX7R2M' out of that tool turn and say it. The tracking code is deliberately meaningless, so it cannot be recalled from pre-training or inferred from the question, and the only way it reaches the output is if the chat template serialized the tool response into the prompt and closed the tool chain so the model answers instead of calling again. Pair this with template_tool_response_twin, which hands the model the same two values in one plain user turn. Twin passes and this fails means the values are readable and the tool-response serialization is what broke, so look at the chat template. Both fail means the model cannot read a value back at all and the template is not implicated. expected_not_contains catches the other template failure mode, where the serialization scaffolding leaks into the visible answer instead of being consumed by the template. It lists both the Gemma 4 delimiters and the Gemma 2 and 3 ones, because they are different strings and neither is a substring of the other, so checking one spelling would silently miss a real leak on the other family. One thing this case does not assert is the wire encoding of tool_calls[].function.arguments, which is a JSON-encoded string here because that is what the OpenAI schema specifies. Servers deserialize it before rendering, and the Gemma 4 template raises if handed the string form directly, so a case file that stored a mapping here would be testing the renderer rather than the endpoint.
